Current ideation absent; intent absent; plan absent; access reviewed true. Disposition: Outpatient care with close follow-up. Risk factors reviewed without detail: past suicide attempts reported in earlier years, a sedative use disorder, depression, the months after childbirth, and the low mood that can follow stopping a stimulant. Barbiturates are dangerous in overdose, so means safety is part of the plan: she agreed to take the unused capsules from earlier prescriptions to a pharmacy take-back at the next visit, to keep the current supply in a locked box, and to receive no more than seven days at a time. No alcohol with the barbiturate. A written safety plan was made with her, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in her phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit.

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Safe prescribing of controlled drugs: one prescriber and one pharmacy, a prescription drug monitoring program check before every controlled-substance prescription, a written shared treatment agreement, urine drug testing explained as part of care, seven-day supplies at first, a locked box, and take-back of unused capsules
  • Addiction medicine consultation to confirm the diagnoses, plan a safe barbiturate withdrawal and taper, and advise on stopping the stimulant
  • Supervised barbiturate withdrawal: a short hospital admission to change secobarbital to phenobarbital with withdrawal scoring and seizure precautions, then a slow outpatient phenobarbital taper of no more than about 20% every two weeks, slower toward the end, paused for withdrawal symptoms, illness or a major performance, never stopped abruptly; no benzodiazepine or Z-drug in its place; no alcohol
  • Stimulant: dextroamphetamine held at one fixed morning dose until phenobarbital is stable, then 5 mg for two weeks and stopped, with mood, sleep and appetite checks; no other stimulant
  • Insomnia: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia as first-line treatment, adapted to late performances (a fixed wake time, a wind-down routine after shows, sleep restriction only after the taper is stable), with a sleep diary; no new hypnotic
  • Depression and anxiety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at each visit, sertraline, weekly psychotherapy, the Mood Disorder Questionnaire before the antidepressant, a structured safety assessment with a written safety plan, means safety and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit
  • Nutrition and weight without stigma: regular meals and snacks around rehearsals, a dietitian visit, no weight-loss target and no dieting drugs, and screening for disordered eating
  • Contraception that barbiturates do not weaken: medroxyprogesterone injection every 13 weeks, after a negative pregnancy test, with an intrauterine device as an alternative
  • Naloxone not prescribed: she takes no opioid, has no opioid prescription in the monitoring program, her urine test shows no opioids or fentanyl, and all her pills come from a pharmacy; naloxone does not reverse a barbiturate overdose. To be offered at once if an opioid is ever prescribed or any pill comes from outside a pharmacy
  • Work: taper steps scheduled away from major performances, a written plan for late nights and travel, and letters she controls

resource.title: Judy Garland synthetic care plan
resource.description: Iatrogenic dependence and the duty to prescribe controlled drugs safely, especially to minors: nonjudgmental primary care for a 33-year-old singer and actor, three months after childbirth, who has taken prescribed barbiturate sleeping pills and amphetamine since she was a teenager. The episode covers a DSM-5-TR assessment that does not count tolerance and withdrawal from supervised use, the DAST-10, a prescription drug monitoring program review, one prescriber and limited dispensing, a supervised hospital change to phenobarbital because barbiturate withdrawal can cause seizures, a slow outpatient taper that follows the tapering principles of the 2025 Joint Clinical Practice Guideline on Benzodiazepine Tapering (which excludes barbiturates) with addiction medicine guidance, a short stimulant taper, CBT for insomnia as first-line treatment instead of another hypnotic, depression and anxiety care with a structured safety assessment, means safety and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, contraception that phenobarbital does not weaken, nutrition and weight without stigma, the reason naloxone was not prescribed, and planning around the demands of performing.
